title: Scroll-Settle, Fluid Units, Counters, Focus Rings & CloseWatcher
description: Five browser-native drops: a scrollend-triggered gallery, container-query-unit fluid scaling, custom @counter-style numbering, a morphing focus ring, and CloseWatcher-driven dismissible surfaces.

drops.title: Scroll-Settle Gallery
drops.description: Cards stay still while you scroll and pop into a settled glow the instant scrolling actually stops.
drops.concept: Instead of binding animation to a continuous CSS scroll-timeline (the dominant 2026 pattern, shown for contrast in a live progress bar underneath), this drop listens for the discrete scrollend event and only then figures out which snap-card is centered and fires a one-shot settle animation — a pop, scale and glow pulse. Browsers without native scrollend fall back to a tuned scroll-debounce that behaves identically, with a status line showing which path fired.
drops.source: Inspired by MDN's Element: scrollend event reference

interaction.mouse: Scroll the rail with a wheel or drag; watch the compare bar move continuously while the card only settles once you stop
interaction.touch: Swipe the rail; the settle fires once your finger lifts and momentum ends

drops.title: Fluid Container Units
drops.description: One card's type scale, icon and padding are sized in cqi — they reflow with its own box, not the viewport.
drops.concept: Container query length units (cqi/cqw/cqh) let an element size itself relative to its nearest container-type: inline-size ancestor instead of the viewport. This drop puts an identical widget twice — one sized entirely in cqi inside a draggable-width box, one sized in vw for contrast — so dragging the handle visibly reflows only the cqi version, while resizing the browser window only moves the vw version. A live readout shows the current 1cqi-to-pixel conversion.
drops.source: Inspired by MDN's CSS container query length units reference

interaction.mouse: Drag the vertical handle to resize the green card's box
interaction.click: Preset buttons snap to Narrow/Medium/Wide widths
interaction.touch: Drag the handle with a finger; presets are tap-friendly

drops.title: Counter Foundry
drops.description: Four custom @counter-style numbering systems power a real step-list — no JavaScript renders a single digit.
drops.concept: The @counter-style at-rule lets CSS define entirely custom list markers — fixed symbol sets, numeric positional systems (used here for a hex-style counter), and additive systems (used for compact Roman numerals) — all wired up purely through list-style. A live builder panel takes a space-separated symbol string and a suffix, generates a fresh @counter-style custom-style rule as text, and injects it into a <style> tag so you can watch your own emoji or glyph set become real ordered-list markers.

interaction.mouse: Click a tab to switch counter styles; type in the builder fields to generate your own
interaction.touch: Tabs and text fields are fully tap-friendly

drops.title: Magic Focus Ring
drops.description: One shared ring glides between a nav, icon buttons and a wide row, morphing its size and corner radius each time.
drops.concept: Rather than styling outline per-element, a single absolutely-positioned ring listens for focusin across the page, reads the newly-focused element's getBoundingClientRect() and computed border-radius, and transitions its own left/top/width/height/border-radius to match on a springy overshoot curve — a FLIP-style morph applied continuously to real keyboard and pointer focus, not a scripted demo sequence. A panel toggle restricts it to :focus-visible only, matching real keyboard-navigation etiquette.
drops.source: Inspired by CSS-Tricks' "Animated Position of Focus Ring"

interaction.mouse: Click any pill or card to send focus there
interaction.keyboard: Tab/Shift+Tab through every element and watch the ring follow

drops.title: Close-Watched Surfaces
drops.description: A bottom sheet, drawer and dialog all dismiss through a real CloseWatcher — Escape and back-gesture both just work.
drops.concept: The CloseWatcher Web API lets any custom overlay hook into the platform's own 'close' gesture — Escape on desktop, the Android back button on mobile — without a hand-rolled keydown listener, and exposes a cancelable cancel event before the close event fires. This drop wires three overlays to real CloseWatcher instances: a plain drawer and dialog close immediately, while a bottom sheet with unsaved text calls preventDefault() on the first cancel to show an inline discard-confirmation, then lets the second close request through. Unsupported browsers fall back to an equivalent Escape-key listener with the same cancel/close semantics, logged live in the side panel either way.
drops.source: Inspired by MDN's CloseWatcher Web API reference

interaction.mouse: Open a surface, then press Escape instead of the close button
interaction.click: Buttons open/close each surface; backdrop click also requests a close
interaction.touch: Tap to open; on mobile, the back gesture fires the same close-watcher event
